answer: Each bridge seat starts with pier ownership: a single named footing in the open ocean, where every epoch the operator clamps a registered quartz slab and logs the piezoelectric charge the tide drives into it. Beside the barnacle ring on a marked patch, that reading encodes the footing's water history; it can't be precomputed, and last epoch's photo fails as the ring grows. Two seats on one pier emit identical traces and are slashed. A sybil needs a second footing, crystal, logger and an operator at both tides, costs that grow with each fake identity while per-seat yield stays flat.
